clue.text: Guide to behaviour

definitions.meaning: to guide is to lead or steer, as a maestro steers an orchestra
the way a person acts, as in a school report's mark for it

explanation.surface: The title of a manual of etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb meaning to lead or direct and a noun for a person's manners or deportment.

clue.text: Accountant raising the wind holding party in restaurant

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the first pieces wrap round the word for party

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means lifting the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: air is a wind or breeze
a fete is a festive gathering

explanation.surface: An accountant hosting a party in a diner and causing a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raising' reads a word upwards; 'holding' sets the party inside, after the accountant's letters. 'wind' is moving air, not a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service eating place.

clue.text: Just beginning to cause a new rising

parts.note: an ascent is a rise

explanation.surface: Someone just starting to stir up another revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cause a' are link words; 'rising' is a climb, not a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerging or coming into being.

clue.text: The City Road follows this to and fro

definitions.meaning: from the rhyme 'Pop Goes the Weasel', which goes 'along the City Road' in this manner

explanation.surface: A London street that runs back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: City Road is a street in London named in the nursery song 'Pop Goes the Weasel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means going back and forth, and the song's line names this very route on City Road.

clue.text: Listen to hard rock

indicators.note: listen to signals that we want a word sounding like the word for hard

parts.note: tough means hard

explanation.surface: Advice to hear some heavy rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' is stone, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock made of consolidated volcanic ash.

clue.text: The sign of a prodigy

definitions.meaning: an omen or warning of what is coming
in its older sense, a marvel taken as an omen of events

explanation.surface: Someone spotting the telltale mark of a child genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prodigy' suggests a gifted child, but its older meaning is a wonder or omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name an omen, a marvel foreshadowing some momentous event.

clue.text: Commonplace old character, first in the field

annotationWithheld.why: Commonplace old character, first in the field (10): no parse found; PHI (old character) leaves LISTINE unaccounted for and no source confirms the wordplay.
annotationWithheld.clue: Commonplace old character, first in the field

clue.text: It goes round 3

indicators.note: the cross-reference brings in the solution to 3 down, meaning a word that reads the same whichever way you go along this down light

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A cryptic pointer to something that spins.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to the answer of 3 down: this word reads the same up and down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Committed money upfront

definitions.meaning: a deposit paid as a pledge

explanation.surface: A deposit paid in advance to seal a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Means serious and sincere, and also a deposit paid to secure a bargain.

clue.text: Drink, divine in trifle

indicators.note: in places the word for divine inside the word for trifle

parts.note: to toy is to trifle; a toy is a trifle
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a divine, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A drink served in a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a clergyman; 'trifle' is a plaything, not dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot whisky punch with sugar and water.

clue.text: A sure sign initially of recurring depression

indicators.note: recurring means running back, so the collected letters are read in the opposite direction
initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor noting that a returning low mood is a reliable symptom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'A sure sign', ASS, then 'of' joins whole; 'recurring' turns ASSOF round. 'Depression' is a hollow, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy this is a pit or hollow in a bone, a physical dip rather than low spirits.

clue.text: Fried food a journalist wasted

parts.note: a fritter is a piece of food coated in batter and fried
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter squandering time eating doughnuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away money or time is to squander it bit by bit.

clue.text: Stylish conclusion in essay

indicators.note: in places the word for conclusion inside the word for essay

parts.note: an essay in its older sense is an attempt, a try
a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: A teacher praising an elegant final paragraph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a piece of writing, but here it means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fashionable and up to date is described as stylish.

clue.text: It's intensely hot going round the centre of Barcelona

indicators.note: going round says the word for hot encircles the other piece

parts.note: fiery means hot, burning

indicators.note: the centre of picks out the middle three letters of the Spanish city's name

explanation.surface: A heatwave report on central Barcelona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of' takes the middle three letters of the nine in BARCELONA, and 'going round' wraps the word for hot about them. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with fury or great force, as a battle raging with ferocity.

clue.text: Leaving parade quarrelling

explanation.surface: Soldiers bickering as they leave a march.
explanation.definitionFit: A military drill term for stepping out of ranks, and an idiom for an argument.

clue.text: Cut down allowance to a relation

indicators.note: cut down means the word for allowance is docked of its final letter

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance, as of food

explanation.surface: Someone trimming the pocket money paid to a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' looks like a relative, but here it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics this is the proportional relationship between two quantities.

clue.text: Car worker admitting to being an unthinking person

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word for worker takes the next piece inside

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a hired hand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car plant employee confessing to being mindless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot or anyone acting mechanically without thought is likened to a machine.

clue.text: Decoration for mettle is nothing out of the ordinary

indicators.note: out of the ordinary says these letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the zero

explanation.surface: Bravery being rewarded with an unremarkable medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the ordinary' rearranges METTLE IS plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas plant hung up as seasonal ornament.

clue.text: Get advice on questions in The Times, possibly

parts.note: advices, in an older sense, is news, information
an exam paper is a set of questions

explanation.surface: Consulting a newspaper for help on puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advices' was once a common word for news from abroad. 'Get' and 'in' are links; 'on' places questions second.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is an example of a daily publication.

clue.text: Hormone treatment for an ideal Royal Navy?

indicators.note: treatment is a working-over, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking what hormone therapy would make the perfect navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment for' rearranges AN IDEAL plus RN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands secrete this hormone in fight-or-flight situations.

clue.text: Call for a time of prayer

definitions.meaning: a bugle call ordering a withdrawal
a spell of seclusion for prayer and meditation

explanation.surface: Announcing a prayer session.
explanation.definitionFit: A military bugle signal, and a religious period of contemplation.

clue.text: One used to take a drink, undiluted, on the way

definitions.text: One used to take a drink

indicators.note: on here means following, placing the word for undiluted after the abbreviation for way

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
raw spirits are neat, not watered down

explanation.surface: A drinker taking whisky neat while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin tube through which one sips a beverage.

clue.text: Soldiers conceal move to new position

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers
to plant is to hide, as in planting evidence

explanation.surface: Troops concealing something and shifting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Transplanting a seedling to a new bed.

clue.text: Attractive fine print

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
an etching is a print made from an etched plate

explanation.surface: Praising a pretty, delicate engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming or good-looking, as in a becoming outfit.

clue.text: Panel built up in mosaic — a fake!

indicators.note: built up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone spots a forged mosaic panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden letters; 'built up' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia board above a shop window or a car dashboard.

clue.text: Source of heroin found on island — one in a republic

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an ait is a small river island
I is one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Drugs smuggled in a republic on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: An ait or eyot is a small island in the River Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean country occupying part of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Blunder by fielder in erect position

parts.note: slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, and the player there
standing upright is being up

explanation.surface: A cricketer making an error while standing tall.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a slip is a fielder stationed just behind the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or careless error.

clue.text: Doctor sues customs

indicators.note: to doctor is to alter or tamper, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician taking the customs office to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits or practices.

clue.text: To cure sin, perhaps, is simple

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words may be another arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether curing sin is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TO CURE SIN. 'Simple' means foolish, not easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid or dim-witted, as 'simple' once meant mentally slow.

clue.text: Ship reversing into Liverpool, perhaps, with skill

indicators.note: reversing means the assembled letters run backwards

parts.note: Lord Liverpool was a British Prime Minister, so he is an example of a PM
art means skill or craft

explanation.surface: A vessel backing into the Merseyside port with dexterity.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool here is Lord Liverpool, Prime Minister 1812-27, not the port; 'reversing' turns PMART round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp steamer is a cargo vessel with no fixed route.

clue.text: Strike to achieve closure of plant

parts.note: to attain is to achieve

indicators.note: closure of means the end, the final letter, of the following word

explanation.surface: Workers walking out to force a factory shutdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' is the archaic verb meaning to strike or touch, not industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to hit or touch, and later to taint or condemn.

clue.text: Noisy fellow putting gun to one side

parts.note: the Sten was a British submachine gun
taken as written
R, for right, is one side

explanation.surface: A loud man laying down his weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek herald in the Iliad with a voice as loud as fifty men, so any loud-voiced person.
